mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following low UNRATE, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 4.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day periods following FEDFUNDS crossing above 4.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) coupled with falling federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) may indicate stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following rising CPIAUCSL and falling FEDFUNDS, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) during a late-cycle expansion indicates a potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day periods following a decline in HOUST, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong supply-side activity, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 5-day periods following an increase in INDPRO, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following a significant increase in PAYEMS, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) combined with rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day periods following a slowdown in GDPC1 and rising UNRATE, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary easing cycle indicates lower borrowing costs, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following a decrease in FEDFUNDS, this hypothesis is falsified.
